jerusalem-2017-12-18-record-reconstructi.draft/slip: The provision regarding Jerusalem and diplomatic missions was contained within Egypt's unadopted draft S/2017/1060. Submitted on 18 December 2017 at meeting S/PV.8139 by the Group of Arab States, the draft received 14 votes in favor and one against from the United States. The Security Council chair declared it unadopted due to the permanent member's negative vote, resulting in no new Council obligations.
jerusalem-2017-12-18-record-reconstructi.draft/matched: Operative paragraph 1 of Egypt's unadopted draft S/2017/1060 proposed declaring decisions altering Jerusalem's character, status, or demographic composition ineffective and calling for their rescission. It also mandated States to refrain from establishing diplomatic missions in Jerusalem, citing resolution 478 (1980). This proposal, presented at meeting S/PV.8139 on 18 December 2017, received 14 votes in favour and one against from the United States. The draft was unadopted due to the negative vote of a permanent member and created no new Council obligations.
jerusalem-2017-12-18-record-reconstructi.united_states/slip: At meeting S/PV.8139 on 18 December 2017, the Security Council considered Egypt's draft resolution on Jerusalem. The draft received 14 votes in favour and one against from the United States. Chairperson declared it unadopted due to the negative vote of a permanent member. Nikki Haley provided the United States' national explanation for this vote. The failed draft created no new Council obligations.
jerusalem-2017-12-18-record-reconstructi.united_states/matched: Nikki Haley explained the U.S. negative vote, stating the veto defended American sovereignty and its role in the Middle East peace process. She asserted the U.S. decides embassy location. Haley distinguished recognition from final status and boundaries, noting recognition does not prejudge the city's status or boundaries to be negotiated by the parties. This explanation followed the Security Council's rejection of Egypt's draft on Jerusalem on 18 December 2017.
jerusalem-2017-12-18-record-reconstructi.united_kingdom/slip: At meeting S/PV.8139 on 18 December 2017, the Security Council considered Egypt's draft resolution on Jerusalem. It received 14 votes in favour and one against from the United States, which was the sole negative vote. The chair declared the draft unadopted due to this permanent member's opposition, creating no new Council obligations. Matthew Rycroft provided the United Kingdom's explanation for its affirmative vote.
jerusalem-2017-12-18-record-reconstructi.united_kingdom/matched: Matthew Rycroft explained the UK's affirmative vote on 18 December 2017, stating the draft aligned with prior Council resolutions and the UK's established position. He advocated for negotiated status with Jerusalem serving as the capital of both States. Rycroft disagreed with US recognition and embassy relocation, noting the British Embassy remains in Tel Aviv with no relocation plans. The draft was unadopted due to the US negative vote, creating no new obligations.

It received 14 votes in favour, one against from the United States, and no abstentions. The draft was unadopted due to the US negative vote by a permanent member, creating no new Council obligations. Olof Skoog provided Sweden's national explanation for its affirmative vote.
jerusalem-2017-12-18-record-reconstructi.sweden/matched: At meeting S/PV.8139 on 18 December 2017, Sweden's Olof Skoog explained its affirmative vote on Egypt's draft regarding Jerusalem. Skoog stated that final status must be negotiated per relevant UN resolutions, supported the restriction on diplomatic missions under resolution 478 (1980), and distinguished the failed draft from earlier adopted resolutions. The draft received 14 votes in favour and one against from the United States. The Security Council chair declared it unadopted due to the permanent member's negative vote, creating no new Council obligations.
